<!-- Generated by tools/docgen from doc comments. Do not edit: run scripts/docs.sh. -->

```odin
import audiofile "fire:audiofile"
```

Reading and writing audio files.

WAV (including RF64/BW64 and WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE) and AIFF/AIFC are read
and written by this package itself, with no C code. FLAC, MP3 and Ogg Vorbis
are decoded by `fire:audiofile/codecs`, which returns the same `Reader`.

Readers deliver planar f32 whatever the file's encoding, and seek to any
frame. A reader allocates its buffers when it opens, so `read` and `seek`
never allocate: a disk-streaming thread can use them freely. They do block on
file I/O, so never call them on the audio thread.

```odin
r, err := audiofile.open("drums.wav")
if err != .None do return
defer audiofile.close(r)
info := audiofile.info(r)
left := make([]f32, info.frames)
right := make([]f32, info.frames)
audiofile.read(r, {left, right}, int(info.frames))
```

Writers are made for recording: the header is brought up to date every
second of audio by default, so a crash leaves a playable file, and a WAV that
grows past 4 GB becomes RF64 in place.

```odin
w, _ := audiofile.writer_create("take.wav", audiofile.default_writer_settings(48_000, 2))
audiofile.writer_write(w, {left, right}, frames)
audiofile.writer_close(w)
```

See /guides/audio-files/ for more.

## Types

### Format

```odin
Format :: enum u8 {
	Unknown,
	Wav,
	Aiff,
	Flac,
	Mp3,
	Ogg_Vorbis,
}
```

A container format.

| Value | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `Unknown` |  |
| `Wav` | RIFF/WAVE, RF64 or BW64 |
| `Aiff` | AIFF or AIFC |
| `Flac` |  |
| `Mp3` |  |
| `Ogg_Vorbis` |  |

### Sample_Format

```odin
Sample_Format :: enum u8 {
	Int8,
	Int16,
	Int24,
	Int32,
	Float32,
	Float64,
	Compressed,
}
```

How samples are stored in a file.

| Value | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `Int8` |  |
| `Int16` |  |
| `Int24` |  |
| `Int32` |  |
| `Float32` |  |
| `Float64` |  |
| `Compressed` | FLAC, MP3, Ogg Vorbis |

### Info

```odin
Info :: struct {
	format: Format,
	encoding: Sample_Format,
	bits: int,
	sample_rate: f64,
	channels: int,
	frames: i64,
	recovered: bool,
}
```

What `open` found out about a file.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `format` |  |
| `encoding` |  |
| `bits` | bits per sample as stored; 0 for compressed formats |
| `sample_rate` | Hz |
| `channels` |  |
| `frames` | length in sample frames |
| `recovered` | the header disagreed with the file (for instance after a crash while recording); `frames` is what the file actually holds |

### Error

```odin
Error :: enum u8 {
	None,
	Not_Found,
	Io_Error,
	Unsupported_Format,
	Corrupt,
	Invalid_Argument,
	Out_Of_Memory,
	Too_Large,
}
```

Result of file operations.

| Value | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `None` |  |
| `Not_Found` | no such file, or no permission to open it |
| `Io_Error` | reading or writing failed |
| `Unsupported_Format` | not a format this package (or codecs) reads, or an encoding it doesn't support |
| `Corrupt` | the file is damaged or truncated beyond use |
| `Invalid_Argument` | a bad setting or out-of-range position |
| `Out_Of_Memory` |  |
| `Too_Large` | an AIFF writer reached the format's 4 GB limit |

### Reader

```odin
Reader :: struct {...}
```

A file opened for reading. Create with `open` (or `codecs.open`); free with
`close`. Not safe to use from two threads at once. Fields are internal.

### Reader_VTable

```odin
Reader_VTable :: struct {
	read: proc(r: ^Reader, out: [][]f32, frames: int) -> (int, Error),
	seek: proc(r: ^Reader, frame: i64) -> Error,
	close: proc(r: ^Reader),
}
```

The operations behind a `Reader`, for decoder packages such as
`fire:audiofile/codecs` that make readers with `reader_make`.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `read` | Decode up to `frames` frames into `out` (one slice per channel, each at least `frames` long), returning how many were decoded: fewer only at the end of the file. |
| `seek` | Move to frame `frame` (0 ..= info.frames). |
| `close` | Free the decoder's state (but not the Reader itself). |

### Writer_Settings

```odin
Writer_Settings :: struct {
	format: Format,
	encoding: Sample_Format,
	sample_rate: f64,
	channels: int,
	dither: bool,
	header_interval: i64,
	rf64_threshold: i64,
}
```

How `writer_create` writes a file. Start from `default_writer_settings`.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `format` | .Wav or .Aiff (float AIFF is written as AIFC) |
| `encoding` | .Int16, .Int24, .Int32, .Float32 or .Float64 |
| `sample_rate` | Hz, a whole number |
| `channels` | 1 ..= 65535 |
| `dither` | add TPDF dither when writing 16-bit |
| `header_interval` | Frames between header updates while writing. A crash then loses at most this much from the header's point of view (the reader recovers the rest from the file size anyway). 0 = only at `writer_close`. |
| `rf64_threshold` | WAV only: when the RIFF size would exceed this many bytes the file is turned into RF64 in place. 0 means the format's limit (4 GiB); lower it only to test RF64 handling. |

### Writer

```odin
Writer :: struct {...}
```

A file being written. Create with `writer_create`, finish with
`writer_close`. Writing blocks on I/O: use it from a disk thread, never
the audio thread. Fields are internal.

## Procedures

### reader_make

```odin
reader_make :: proc(vtable: ^Reader_VTable, data: rawptr, info: Info, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> (^Reader, Error)
```

For decoder packages: makes a reader around `data` and `vtable`. `close`
calls `vtable.close` and then frees the reader with `allocator`.

### open

```odin
open :: proc(path: string, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> (^Reader, Error)
```

Opens a WAV or AIFF file for reading. Allocates its buffers now; free with
`close`. Use `codecs.open` to also open FLAC, MP3 and Ogg Vorbis.

### info

```odin
info :: proc(r: ^Reader) -> Info
```

What the file is: format, encoding, rate, channels and length.

### position

```odin
position :: proc(r: ^Reader) -> i64
```

The frame the next `read` starts at.

### read

```odin
read :: proc(r: ^Reader, out: [][]f32, frames: int) -> (n: int, err: Error)
```

Decodes up to `frames` frames from the current position into `out`, as
planar f32 in -1..1. `out` needs one slice per channel, each at least
`frames` long; extra slices are left alone, and with fewer slices than
channels the remaining channels are skipped. Returns how many frames were
read: fewer than asked only at the end of the file. Never allocates;
blocks on I/O.

### seek

```odin
seek :: proc(r: ^Reader, frame: i64) -> Error
```

Moves to frame `frame` (0 ..= `info(r).frames`). Exact for every format.

### close

```odin
close :: proc(r: ^Reader)
```

Closes the file and frees the reader.

### bytes_per_sample

```odin
bytes_per_sample :: proc "contextless"(e: Sample_Format) -> int
```

Bytes per sample of a PCM encoding (0 for `.Compressed`).

### default_writer_settings

```odin
default_writer_settings :: proc(sample_rate: f64, channels: int) -> Writer_Settings
```

24-bit WAV, header updated every second of audio, dither on (for 16-bit).

### writer_create

```odin
writer_create :: proc(path: string, settings: Writer_Settings, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> (w: ^Writer, err: Error)
```

Creates (or replaces) `path` and writes a header for an empty file.
Free with `writer_close`.

### writer_write

```odin
writer_write :: proc(w: ^Writer, input: [][]f32, frames: int) -> Error
```

Appends `frames` frames from `input` (one slice per channel, each at least
`frames` long). Samples are clipped to -1..1 for integer encodings.
Allocates nothing; blocks on I/O.

### writer_frames

```odin
writer_frames :: proc(w: ^Writer) -> i64
```

Frames written so far.

### writer_close

```odin
writer_close :: proc(w: ^Writer) -> (err: Error)
```

Finishes the header, closes the file and frees the writer (even when it
returns an error).
